But as its eternal ground or the substratum that was never within the cycle.
This unmanifest, it is unmanifest because no indriya, mind, buddhi can grasp it as an object.
It is beyond all objects and ajinti rupa, inconceivable form.

Sankaracharya now identifies the two avyattas as the same.
The nirguna avyatta as sanatana, which is nirguna paramatman or akshara brahma.
In the Swaroopa, the saguna avyatta is maya or prakriti in pralaya avastha, that is in the night or the deep sleep.
Whereas the nirguna avyatta, akshara brahman or paramatman, that is the Swaroopa.
And what are the dharma?
Dharma of saguna avyatta is, it goes through the cycles with kalpas, punaravarti, birth and death.
Whereas the nirguna avyatta is sanatana, sadhanootana, beyond all cycles.
Ever new.
And lakshana, if you want, if you consider the lakshana between the two,
the saguna avyatta is called avyatta, whereas the nirguna avyatta is actual avyatta.
That is why, when we are in deep sleep,
even though we are in deep sleep, it is considered that we have become one with the sattva.

The sambandha between the two is called kārya-kāraṇa within māyā but as ādiṣṭhāna.
